1.10A.description: O₂/N₂/Ar produced via air separation and delivered via pipeline or bulk liquid logistics; includes on-site generation/ownership models. A co-located "infrastructure plant" category with distinct capex and contracting.

1.10B.name: Electronics specialty gases, ultra-high purity gases, and mixtures
1.10B.description: High-purity gases and mixtures used in deposition/etch/clean/anneal plus dopants and sensitive chemistries. Cylinder/ISO delivery, specialty purification/blending, traceability, QA, and safety systems create a separate supplier universe from bulk.

1.11.name: Bulk construction and structural materials
1.11.description: Cement/concrete, structural steel, aluminum, aggregates, rebar, specialty coatings. Massive consumption for datacenters, substations, cooling infrastructure, fab shells; cost-significant at buildout scale even when not the gating constraint.

1.12.name: Engineered fluids, fluoropolymers, and specialty chemicals
1.12.description: Dielectric coolants for immersion and direct-to-chip systems, fluoropolymer tubing/seals, specialty refrigerants, and regulatory-sensitive formulations. Chemistry complexity and potential restrictions can strand cooling architectures.

companies.name: Haohua Chemical Science & Technology Corp., Ltd.

1.13.name: Water as an industrial input
1.13.description: Supply, treatment, recycling/reclaim, and wastewater discharge for fabs, datacenters, and thermal power. Includes water rights acquisition/access and permitting constraints that increasingly gate siting and expansion.

1.2.name: Copper smelting & refining (concentrate → cathode)
1.2.description: Pyrometallurgical conversion of concentrate into blister copper and/or cast anodes (smelting), followed by electrorefining to cathode and hydrometallurgical routes including SX/EW (refining). Smelting involves emissions/permitting, sulfur capture, and energy intensity; refining is the cathode-grade purity gate that feeds electrical equipment, wiring, PCBs, and thermal systems. Treatment charges (TC) and refining charges (RC) are the key midstream pricing mechanisms. Combined as a single discovery node because vertically integrated operators dominate and the company universe overlaps heavily.

1.3.description: Conversion into engineered copper products used in datacenter electrical distribution, transformers, connectors, and electronics (including copper foil for PCBs and packaging). Includes recycling and secondary processing (scrap collection/sorting, secondary smelting/refining, remelt) as a feedstock pathway into the same semi-fabrication operations. Often a different operator universe from mining/refining.
